title: TTP and Clinical Failure Outcomes
text:
In the v1 analysis (n=57 studies, Feb 2026), the clinical failure analysis was deemed not feasible: only 4 studies had usable data, with severe directionality contradictions and one extreme outlier (OR≈1115 in Melling 2019). The v4 update adds 43 new strict-pool studies, several of which report persistent bacteremia, microbiological clearance, or relapse outcomes. This page revisits feasibility.

title: Time-to-Positivity and Mortality in Bacteremia
text:
Primary analysis (strict pool): 100 studies contributing 72 mortality effect sizes.
Sensitivity analysis (strict + inclusive pool): 140 studies, 84 effect sizes.






ImportantPrimary result (strict pool)



Pooled odds ratio for mortality (short vs long TTP):

OR = 2.06 (95% CrI: 1.67–2.55)

Probability that shorter TTP increases mortality: 100.0%

Between-study heterogeneity: I² = 62%, τ = 0.69










TipSensitivity result (n=140)



Including the 40 inclusive-pool studies: OR = 1.92 (95% CrI: 1.58–2.35), P(harm) = 100.0%, I² = 63%.

title: Time-to-Positivity and Mortality in Bacteremia
text:
2.1 Data source
The analysis dataset is data/TTP_MetaAnalysis_Extraction_Complete_v4.xlsx. Effect sizes (log odds ratios) were computed using metafor::escalc():

2×2 tables when events/totals by TTP category are reported (preferred when available)
Back-calculated from reported OR/HR/RR with 95% CI when 2×2 unavailable
Per-hour estimates (continuous TTP) reported separately

The full effect-size pipeline is in R/01_prepare_data.R.

title: Time-to-Positivity and Mortality in Bacteremia
text:
2.2 Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis
Primary model (specified in R/02_fit_models.R):
\[y_i \mid \text{SE}_i \sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(\mu + u_s,\,\text{SE}_i^2\right),\quad u_s \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tau^2)\]
with weakly-informative priors \(\mu \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)\), \(\tau \sim \text{Half-Cauchy}(0,0.5)\), moderator coefficients \(\mathcal{N}(0,0.5)\). Fitted with brms 4×4000 iterations (1000 warm-up), adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12.

title: Risk of bias (QUIPS)
text:
Risk of bias was assessed with the QUIPS tool (Hayden et al. 2013), scoring six domains 1 (low), 2 (moderate), 3 (high):

Study participation (selection bias)
Study confounding (multivariable adjustment for key confounders)
Outcome measurement (ascertainment / objectivity)
Statistical analysis (appropriateness, reporting completeness)
Attrition (loss to follow-up, missing data)
Prognostic factor measurement (TTP measurement quality)

Overall rating follows QUIPS guidance — worst-domain-dominates, not arithmetic mean. See references/QUIPS_scoring_guide.md in the extraction skill for the project-specific rubric.

title: Methods & PRISMA flow
text: Figure 1: Updated PRISMA flow for v4 database

title: Methods & PRISMA flow
text:
3.1 Strict (primary pool, n=100 studies)
A study qualifies if all of the following hold:

Population: adult bacteremia, candidemia, or other bloodstream infection confirmed by blood culture
Exposure: TTP (time to blood culture positivity) measured by an automated continuous-monitoring system
Outcome: at least one clinical outcome reported — mortality, persistent bacteremia, microbiological clearance, or relapse
Quantitative TTP↔︎outcome association: 2×2 table by TTP category, OR/HR/RR with CI, or β-per-hour with SE

Studies that report TTP and outcomes only descriptively (without a quantitative TTP↔︎outcome model) are excluded under the strict criterion.

title: Methods & PRISMA flow
text:
3.2 Inclusive (sensitivity pool, n=140 studies)
Loosens criterion (4): a paper qualifies if TTP and a clinical outcome are both reported in the same cohort, even if not cross-tabulated. Inclusive-only studies are flagged with [INCLUSIVE_ONLY] in tbl_study.notes and are used only in sensitivity analyses.

title: Methods & PRISMA flow
text:
3.3 Standing exclusions (both pools)

Narrative review, case report (n<10), editorial, conference abstract only, study protocol
TTP not measured (e.g., duration-of-bacteremia in days, time-to-antibiotic, transit time)
TTP used solely as part of a CRBSI case definition ([CONTAMINATED_TTP] flag)
Population not BSI
Full text not in English and not extractable

NoteInterpreting Egger’s test in this context



Egger’s test has known limitations when between-study heterogeneity is high (as here): the test can flag asymmetry that reflects genuine heterogeneity rather than publication bias. An intercept materially different from zero should be followed up by examining whether small-study effects correlate with identifiable moderators (e.g., pathogen class, adjustment status) before attributing asymmetry to selective reporting.
